correctness.rationale: For n>=1, a homogeneous N+2 square matrix is unimodularly equivalent to the ordinary affine volume determinant. Missing barycentric layers force determinant zero. Otherwise subtraction of one row per layer reduces exactly to the determinant of two square difference vectors; two extra rows permit only one tripled label or two doubled labels. A tripled label contributes N*4^N determinant-one sets. Among the 36 ordered square-segment pairs at doubled layers exactly 10 have determinant zero, 24 have absolute determinant one and 2 have absolute determinant two. These calculations prove H0,H1,H2 and classify all vertex-supported equality sets. The absolute affine determinant is separately convex, so its maximum over arbitrary product points occurs at vertices. The affine volume Jacobian gives ratio 2/((n+1)(n+2)) for every nondegenerate simplex and parallelogram. Exact fraction-free integer enumeration confirms all 70, 792, 8008, 77520 subsets for n=1,2,3,4 with the predicted counts. These finite checks do not replace the all-n proof. No classification of nonvertex maximizers is asserted.

value.rationale: The Cartesian product Δ_n×Q is a natural infinite class of simplotopes already motivated by triangulation and simplex-volume classes. A complete exact volume histogram at every n, all vertex-supported equality configurations, and the sharp unrestricted largest-simplex volume ratio provide intrinsically meaningful, affine-invariant benchmarks. They explain why the known n=2 class-two count equals 24 and give exact counts and ratios beyond that isolated case. The result is not based on arbitrary numerical slices or a mere relabeling of the n=2 result; the all-n structural determinant reduction and multiplicity counts are necessary. No optimal triangulation size is claimed, and volume-only covering implications are explicitly identified as generally nonoptimal.
